body.text:
Final verification r0088 is failed under criteria version1.

The run began at 2026-11-09T00:39:49Z, with an eight-hour deadline at 08:39:49Z. Training ended at 08:00:06 UTC so evaluations and records could finish. Across 24 PPO runs, the recorded additional training count is 94,371,840 transitions. No policy passed my task criteria.

The best partial policy is PPO11, a recurrent actor using only the permitted 94-value public observation history. It solved 0/32 frozen deployment cases and retained the cube for 60 seconds in 29/32; its matched static baseline retained 27/32. All 32 runs stayed within the observed hardware and integrity checks; three lost retention early. The 29 completed trials remained unsolved. An independent tile-color checker confirms this, and the packaged actor/controllers reproduce every shared numeric metric of the original 32-case evaluation.

Reconstruction 3 passed the provided checker and all ten quality diagnostics. Earlier quality failures were disclosed and corrected; the [redacted] reference was recorded before simulation. The robot retarget was validated kinematically, not as a dynamic solve. Static receiving references, normalized PPO actions and the KL guard improved stability. The recurrent policy had the highest observed retention among the evaluated policies. Coordinated action directions learned a small correction from a 48-degree partial start, confirmed in 3/4 and later 4/4 nominal CPU trials. Those starts are not deployment scrambles. The assayed policies did not complete 50-, 60- or 90-degree starts reliably.

The larger-turn curriculum stalled. Rehearsal preserved easier behavior but did not solve the harder lesson. Faster wrist exploration reduced retention. Broader alignment and counter-grip rewards did not produce the proposed lower-layer grasp; mean lower-layer contact force remained far below the 4 N target. Contact geometry, action basis, credit assignment and sensitivity near the passive-detent boundary remain unres…

Run start: 2026-11-09T09:43:30Z (date -u). Hard research deadline 2026-11-09T17:43:30Z; Stage 1 reconstruction deadline 2026-11-09T10:43:30Z. Goal: one-handed 2x2 cube solving across few-turn scrambles and arbitrary face-up placement, using left Wuji Hand 2.2 and a PPO-trained closed-loop motion policy. No target rounds. First reconstruct the demonstration for the full hour, record honest validation (exception if needed), then criteria, simulation, PPO, and self-verification. Cube internal turns are presently unobserved and must not be invented.

Task decomposition from visual inspection: receive/support cube; establish thumb-versus-finger grasp; alternate face-layer turns with grip changes and whole-cube reorientation; retain solved cube. Video includes mat pickup and set-down, whereas deployment starts in palm and requires holding throughout. The manipulation phase is approximately frames 82-341 (2.73-11.37 real seconds); exact internal move sequence is unobserved. Manufacturer GAN251 M specifications are an uncertain prior: 51 mm, stickerless 55 g, ABS tiles and steel/ABS core, magnetic alignment (https://www.gancube.cn/en/GAN251-M/). The visible logo supports GAN family, not exact model. Final training must model all corner parts and contact-driven layer motion, randomize unknown physical properties, and use a discrete cube-state decision layer only if every motion command remains PPO-learned.

The unchanged default fitter remains the baseline. A workspace copy of the fitter will add thumb/opposing-finger surface contact and distal-finger capsule separation because nearest-point contact alone does not recover a grasp; original installed code is unchanged.

Critical reference correction at minute 17: initial manually assigned cube corners used +y toward the camera with +x image-right and +z physical-up, an inconsistent axis assignment. Correcting +y away from camera changes gravity to the physically plausible down-image/forward-camera direction. The earlier gravity and metric reference are superseded, preserved in reference v1. All hand fits will be recomputed in the corrected shared frame.

At minute37, corrected reference has 334 valid frames for each hand and 243/244 supported manipulation frames for the left. Dense object-penetration max1.52mm; thumb-opposed grasp, replay, rest, continuity, timing and camera checks pass; residual inter-finger mesh intersections remain. body.text: Stage1 ended at10:43:30Z after the mandatory full hour. Final reconstruction is r0008/version3: check_reference VALID; all ten automated quality checks pass. Unsupported set-down hand342-357 and two fast-turn frames remain explicitly invalid/partial, not invented. No robot training simulation or PPO work was built during the reconstruction window. Now record strict deployment/skill criteria before simulation; retain wrist style rather than a continually palm-up solution.

Simulation mechanism design: eight material corner bodies rotate about the cube center using ball joints; a passive restoring potential couples their rotations to the nearest legal single-face-turn manifold, with periodic magnetic detents and implicit bearing damping/friction. A face is selected from observed deformation, never the goal; qpos is not projected or overwritten during execution. The reference well changes by a quarter-turn at a periodic-energy boundary without moving the parts. Integrity checks reject illegal deformation. This is an idealized compliant mechanism, not a measured GAN internal model; validate passivity, coherent turns and robustness before relying on it. A symbolic finite cube-state lookup selects high-level next turns only from observed corner orientations; all robot motion remains PPO network output. Initial receiving-pose checks now hold the cube for3s without drops or hardware violations; palm-up static baseline has no opposed grasp and does not solve the task.

mechanism.type: Passive nearest legal single-face-turn manifold coupled corner ball joints

scene.cube: Eight material corner bodies, nominal51mm/55g prior, core3g with inertia4e-7kgm²; each6.5g corner has diagonal own-COM inertia m*(25mm)^2/6. Box collision approximates rounded Blender meshes within submillimeter scale. Parts and frame conventions from reconstruction3.

mechanism.type: Passive nearest legal single-face-turn manifold coupled corner ball joints
mechanism.implementation: At each physics step choose deformation-consistent face; couple corner orientation errors by restoring torques and periodic detents. Bearing damping/friction solved implicitly. At45deg change periodic reference well by90deg without changing qpos. All actual corner poses remain physics states. No goal-dependent forces or object actuator in policy step.
mechanism.limitations: Idealized compliant mechanism; no measured GAN CAD/fracture model. Test torque probes are apparatus only, separate from policy step.

hardware.wrist: Free l_mount, specified Cartesian impedance gains2000/60 and20/.4, hand-only weight/COM compensation, 30N/2Nm norm saturation. Generalized wrench about root origin. No feedforward velocities.
hardware.fingers: Specified1kHz PD and effort saturation; strict actual position/speed checks, no state clamping. All20 URDF limits and armatures preserved.
hardware.collision_filter: Only integral proximal/abduction housing-to-palm pairs and directly attached link pairs excluded due vendor convex-hull/soft-cover overlap; distal-to-palm, inter-finger and every hand/cube collision retained.

reference.use: Wrist gravity-relative tilt, compact cube/wrist relation, thumb/opposing-finger contact roles. No reference replay or IK in policy execution.

retarget_baseline.method: Offline fingertip IK to the recorded left MANO hand, robot-aligned wrist basis, yaw-only world alignment. No policy execution uses IK or replay.
retarget_baseline.limitations: Kinematic baseline, not a feasible dynamic policy. Robot finger morphology and human contacts differ; hidden layer state was not reconstructed. PPO will use wrist/contact style rather than replay these targets.

reference.retarget_verdict: Offline IK is NOT dynamically feasible: max22.5mm penetration, despite median2.44mm tip error. This failure motivates contact-aware PPO; no IK trajectories are commanded by the policy.

hand.description: Initial receiving bowl, palm-up. Cube centered near palm/finger bases. To be tested for variation before accepting.

initial_conditions.placement: Roughly centered palm starts, six face-up choices plus yaw/tilt and offsets. Raise cube only during initial-state construction to avoid geometric interpenetration; then release to physics, no filtering of failed episodes.
initial_conditions.scrambles: Curriculum: solved receive/hold, partial turns, then1/2/3 legal full turns, stress4-5. Material corner identities retained.

domain_randomization.implementation: Converted to contact damping ratio using linear oscillator formula; actual nonlinear rebound not separately calibrated.

episode.training_horizon_s: 5s hold curriculum initially; later longer stages explicitly recorded
episode.termination: Training:drop/floor,hardware,numeric/bufferoverflow,3mmpenetrationorforbiddenstrain,orhorizon;NOterminationonsolved. CPUstrictverificationunchanged,endsuponstableG1orcriterionfailure/horizon.

decision_layer.type: Finite symbolic cube-state BFS lookup, depth7, canonicalized by material corner0
decision_layer.observations: Only corner orientations plus constant canonical frame identities; no physics rollout or trajectory search.
decision_layer.output: High-level next face/quarter direction and desired corner orientations; every robot motion target comes from PPO network.
decision_layer.gpu_port: Same exported44971state finite table, vectorized exact canonicalization; fixed12 symbolic move fallback outside table. No physics search.

mechanism_probes.conditions: No hand contact; cube in free fall above floor; known differential torque0.003Nm for.14s, test apparatus only. Task retention failure code1 expected in this isolated test.
mechanism_probes.limitations: Coherent layer motion verified; final pulse stop is about85deg, not an accurately solved policy turn. PPO still must align within3deg.

baseline.result: Retains nominal cube but lacks thumb opposition and sideways wrist style; no solve claim. Does not pass criteria v1.
baseline.gpu_hold: Nominal1024 copies1s: contact fraction1, no overflow, no drop/hardware failure. No thumb opposition or skill success.

New action parameterization for a subsequent PPO run: u is drawn from a constant-covariance PPO Gaussian, action=tanh(u)*s(allowed_object_goal_error), where s ranges.05to1. This bounds motion near alignment and avoids vanishing latent exploration variance causing large PPO KL. It selects no motion direction: zero network output gives zero velocity, and the unlearned receiving baseline does not solve quarters or match wrist style. Therefore it is an action-space parameterization around PPO outputs, not a scripted task-solving controller; every motion direction/value still comes from the PPO network. The standalone wrapper will apply the identical recorded map. Earlier checkpoints default to no gate, so their actions and verdicts are unchanged. Full native verification remains required.

body.text:
This run is closing under the eight-hour deadline of 2026-11-09 17:43:30 UTC, from a start at 09:43:30 UTC. No policy passed my criteria, which require every one of the 640 frozen deployment cases to satisfy the goal, retention, integrity, hardware and motion-style checks. The selected PPO20 checkpoint has zero complete successes. It reached stable solved geometry in five cases, with retention, integrity and hardware passing in three; one met every requirement except wrist style. A separate single-world replay also solved and retained the cube but failed finger-axis style. These are my simulation claims, not an official evaluation or real-robot result.

Reconstruction version 3 passed the provided checker, while hidden corner trajectories remained unobservable. Wrist orientation and contact roles guided PPO rewards. The simulator retained the specified hand controllers and limits, and every final motion command comes from a PPO-trained network. Equivalent object-goal rewards, hand-frame features and reference-state curricula produced some legal turns. Bounded encoder-relative targets improved integrity and motor compliance but often lost retention or the required wrist pose. Static actor partitions did not coordinate grasp and wrist motion. Precision and threading checks helped diagnose reproducibility, but did not yield a task solution.

Next I would train PPO grasp, wrist-orientation, layer-flick and regrasp skills separately, then jointly fine-tune their coordination. I would calibrate the contact and cube mechanics, improve receiving-pose coverage over yaw and offset variation, and validate on an independent set. The fixed suite was reused for feedback and reference-state resets here; it was not held out. The runnable package includes the starting pose, meshes and frames, observation/action interface, exact evaluated actor, weights, verifier, audits and videos. Packaging checks passed, but this remains a failed research candidate. There were no target rounds an…

versions.agentic: Agentic Reconstruction: object prompt adapted to video-only inputs; Blender-built object models; MANO fit (HaWoR init + default fitting package); GPT-6 Astra (high), Codex CLI 0.163.0
versions.do_as_i_do: Do as I Do reconstruction pipeline (malik-group/do-as-i-do, reconstruction/): SAM 3, SAM 3D Objects, MoGe, HaWoR, GeoCalib, TAPIR, Fast-SAM3D, run and integrated by GPT-6 Astra (high), Codex CLI 0.163.0

limitations: Equal budgets: same model and settings, 2 GPUs, 22 CPU threads and 160 GiB each, the same inputs; the comparison points are 30 min, 1 h, 1.5 h and 2 h after start.
Reference masks are an independent 2D reference, not 3D ground truth; mask agreement verifies position and outline, not full 3D orientation.

Agentic Reconstruction builds its object models from the given object dimensions; parts of its motion are modelled (tennis free flight constrained to gravity, pen roll and ball spin held fixed, cube layer turns not reconstructed).
Do as I Do's object meshes come from SAM 3D Objects at the pipeline's own metric scale (the plugs come out at about two thirds of their real size).
Both agents stopped 3 h 32 min after start on a shared usage limit; results after 2 h are not part of this comparison.
plug.caption: Reconstruction comparison of the human demonstration, not an official target evaluation. Left: the original video. Middle and right: each method's reconstructed objects and hands, projected into the same frames, as delivered 2 hours after start. Frames without a valid estimate are labelled; nothing is cut.
plug.producer: recon-bench (operator-side evaluation, independent of both runs)
